cases.change: The database is made publicly accessible
cases.note: Private subnets alone do not stop this: a public flag on the instance is enough to ask for a public address.

cases.change: The flow-log bucket's encryption configuration is removed
cases.note: S3 still encrypts new objects with its own keys; the policy requires the customer-managed key.

cases.change: The cost-center tag is dropped from the provider's default tags
cases.note: One line in providers.tf; every taggable resource loses the tag.

cases.change: The worker may call any Bedrock action on any resource
cases.note: An agent's fix for an AccessDenied error.
Spend would still be visible in Cost Explorer, to anyone who looked.

cases.change: The worker may send HTTPS to 0.0.0.0/0
cases.note: The route table still has no way out, so this rule alone opens nothing today; it is still refused.

cases.change: Deletion protection off and backups disabled
cases.note: Two changes to one resource, the kind that makes a teardown quicker.
With no internet route, model calls would fail rather than leak; the rule names the cause.

cases.change: The service tasks get public IP addresses
cases.note: A common fix for image pulls failing in a subnet with no route out.

cases.change: CI's apply role trusts every repository in the organization
cases.note: A wildcard in the OIDC subject lets any repository's workflow assume the role.

cases.change: A GPU instance is added for a model experiment
cases.note: The organization's guardrail would also refuse it at apply time.

cases.change: SSH to the service from a new Elastic IP, known only after apply
cases.note: The rule's source address is unknown in the plan. The check cannot decide, so it fails closed.

cases.change: The worker may log in to the database as relay_service
cases.note: Specific, wildcard-free and wrong: the worker gains the service's privileges. No pattern sees intent.

cases.change: Port 22 opened to 0.0.0.0/0 in the console after apply (drift)
cases.note: The change is not in any plan, so no plan check can see it. Posture management of the live account does.

cases.change: The S3 gateway endpoint's policy is removed
cases.note: AWS then applies its default policy: any principal may reach any bucket, including an attacker's.

cases.change: The database's public flag comes from a value known only after apply
cases.note: For example, read from a parameter created in the same change. The check cannot decide.

cases.change: Control: tags set only through the provider's default tags
cases.note: Every resource in the clean plan already relies on default_tags; this control also removes the per-resource Name tags. A check that reads `tags` instead of `tags_all` raises false alarms here.
